newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines 2-year note coupon falls to 11.875 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines 2-year note coupon falls to 11.875 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' two-year fixed rate Treasury notes fetched a lower coupon rate of 11.875 percent at an auction on Tuesday compared with last month's 12.875 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The average rate for the two-year notes was 11.738 percent, with rates ranging from 11.494 to 11.875 percent.
The auction drew 9.580 billion pesos worth of tenders.

The government accepted 4.0 billion pesos worth of bids. Previously, the government only sold 3.0 billion pesos of these two-year notes monthly but it raised the volume in line with its programmed requirements for the early part of the year.
"The fall was deep. It's close to the (11.405 percent) rate of the one-year T-bills," a dealer said.
The slide in the two-year notes came about after short-term rates slumped due to a cut in reserve requirements, traders said.
